resolved_samples.reasoning: Multiple candidates from the results and discussion sections provide strong evidence for both risk and recovery factors. Candidate 5 describes participants' childhood difficulties (risk) and their ability to cope with severe loss and function well despite adversity (recovery). Candidate 6 highlights their action-oriented approach and resilience in the face of illness and loss (recovery). Candidate 8 identifies obstinacy and difficulty accepting help as a problematic personality trait (risk). Candidate 13, from the discussion, summarizes both their vigorous, achieving nature and coping strategies (recovery) as well as their vulnerability due to an inability to adapt to loss of control and closed-off feelings (risk).
